script.speaker: A
script.text: Good morning, Harbourside Community College. How can I help you?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Hello. I'm phoning about the beginners' photography course that starts soon. I wanted to find out if there are any places left.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Yes, we've still got a few places on that one. It's proving quite popular this year. I'll just take a few details, if that's all right. Could I have your surname, please?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, it's Whitcombe.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Sorry, could you spell that for me?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Of course. That's W-H-I-T-C-O-M-B-E.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Lovely, thank you. And your first name is Daniel, isn't it?

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's right.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Thanks, Daniel. And what's the best number to contact you on?

script.speaker: B
script.text: My mobile's best. It's oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, one four three.

script.speaker: A
script.text: So that's oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, one four three.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, that's correct.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Now, do you live in the borough? Residents get a reduced fee, you see.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, I do. I live at twenty-seven Mill Lane, just across from the park.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Mill Lane, that's M-I-L-L, is it?

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's it.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Then you qualify for the resident's rate. The normal fee is ninety-five pounds, but for residents it comes to eighty-five.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Oh, that's good. I thought it would be more. I'm sure the website said a hundred and five.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Ah, that was last year's price. It went down when the college received some extra funding.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Great. And when does the course actually begin? The leaflet I picked up says the seventh of January.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Yes, that's what was printed, but unfortunately we've had to postpone it by a week because the heating system in the main building is being replaced. So the first class will now be on Tuesday the fourteenth of January.

script.speaker: B
script.text: The fourteenth, okay. And is it still at seven in the evening?

script.speaker: A
script.text: It was, but we've changed it to six thirty, so that people can get home at a reasonable time. It finishes at eight thirty, and there's a short break in the middle.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That suits me even better, actually. Do I need to bring any equipment?

script.speaker: A
script.text: Just a camera. It doesn't have to be an expensive one, but it does need to have manual settings, because we spend a lot of time learning how to control the exposure yourself. A phone camera won't be suitable, I'm afraid. We provide tripods, so there's no need to buy one.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Good. I've got an old camera that my brother gave me, so that should do the job.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Perfect. Right, I just have a couple of quick questions for our records. How did you hear about the course? Was it on our website?

script.speaker: B
script.text: No, not the website. My friend Carl did a woodwork course at the college last year and he always speaks highly of it, but it was a poster in the public library that told me about this particular course.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I see, the library. We put posters up there every term. And what made you decide to do photography? Is it for work?

script.speaker: B
script.text: No, nothing like that. My wife and I are going to Iceland in the summer, and I'm tired of my holiday photos looking flat and boring. I'd really like to be able to do the scenery justice.

script.speaker: A
script.text: That sounds like a wonderful trip. Well, you'll learn plenty. One more thing: at the end of the course, students put on a small exhibition of their favourite photographs. It's held in the college café, so friends and family are welcome to come along.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Oh, that sounds brilliant. I'll have to choose carefully!

script.speaker: A
script.text: I'll send a confirmation email today with details of how to pay. You can pay online or at reception.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Wonderful. Thanks very much for your help.

script.speaker: A
script.text: You're welcome, Daniel. We'll see you in January.
